# CAMPFIRE THREAD: POST YOUR BEST ONE (OR YOUR WORST) [color=#5C6B58]Pinned. Stories you were told, stories you tell. Say which it is.[/color]
### #1 ember_keeper (mod) (OP) // 83.03.20 I will start, with the one my crew boss told me my first season on the logging line. Told, not seen.
There is a tall man in the trees who has no voice of his own. He is hungry all the time, and he cannot hunt anything that stays by the fire, so he borrows voices. He listens all day while you work. You call out to your friend, he keeps it. You laugh at a joke, he keeps it. At night, when you have walked away from the fire to piss, he gives your friend's voice back to you from just past the light. [italic]Over here. Come and look at this.[/italic] And you go, because why would you not.
My crew boss said the trick is that he can only say what he has heard. He cannot make up anything new. So if your friend calls you from the dark and says exactly what he said at lunch, word for word, do not go.
### #2 sap_and_saw // 83.03.21 Told: my gran's version is that he was a man once. A man who ate what you should not eat when the supply ship did not come one winter, and it changed him. Made him tall and thin and starving, so the more he eats the hungrier he gets. That is why he is so thin. That is why he follows the camps. She used to say it to stop us wasting food.
### #3 night_logger // 83.03.24 Seen, sort of. I was on a two man felling team, north slope. Night came in early and we were walking out. My partner was about twenty metres ahead of me on the trail, I could see his lamp. And from my left, in the trees, I heard him say my name. His voice, clear, quiet, like he was standing next to me.
His lamp was still twenty metres ahead. Still moving away.
I did not say anything. I walked faster. When I caught him up I asked if he had said anything and he said no, why. Then he said he had heard me say his name, from his right, a minute before. He had not answered either.
### #4 mynah_theory // 83.03.25 Not to ruin the fire, but there are animals on half the worlds out here that mimic sounds. Surveyors have logged at least three species that copy radio chatter. Something in the canopy that copies voices is much more likely than a tall hungry ghost.
### #5 sap_and_saw // 83.03.25 A bird copies a sound. This thing waited until his partner was out of earshot and then used the partner's voice to call him off the trail. That is not copying. That is hunting.
### #6 riverbank_kid // 83.04.02 Seen. I was nine. We were camping by the river past the farms with my mum and my uncle. I heard my mum calling me from the trees on the far side of the water. [italic]Come here, sweetheart, come and see.[/italic] I stood up to go.
My mum was sitting right next to me. She heard it too. She put her hand over my mouth, very hard, and she did not take it away until the sun came up. She has never talked about it. I have never seen her go near those trees again.
### #7 valley_skeptic // 83.04.06 Has anybody noticed when these stories start? My father logged these woods for thirty years. He said the trees had nothing in them bigger than a beetle until the Company put up the research station at the top of the valley. The tall man stories started the same year. Old stories do not usually come with a construction date.
### #8 ember_keeper (mod) // 83.04.06 valley_skeptic is not the first to say this. We are not going to argue it here, there is a thread for it on the front page. But it is worth knowing that my crew boss, the one who told me the story, was a contractor who helped pour the foundations for that station. He told it like a joke. He stopped telling it the year after.
### #9 ember_keeper (mod) // 83.04.29 One more from me, and this one is seen.
Last month a logger on our line went out past the fire to fetch a saw, and a minute later we all heard him shout [italic]help me, help, I am caught.[/italic] Four of us got up. Then he walked back into the light, holding the saw, and asked what we were all staring at.
He had shouted that exact thing the week before, when his sleeve caught in the winch. We had all been there. We had all heard it.
We sat back down. Nobody answered it. It said it nine more times before morning, a little further away each time, and then it said it from right behind the generator. And then it was breathing. Just breathing, slow and wet, like a big man who has walked a long way uphill.
